Freezing rather than exiting preserves the option value of the negotiation track while enrichment and the Hormuz threat remain the only leverage the system has left; at stability 27 the loss frame makes coercive ambiguity rational, but actual closure would strangle my own Chinese lifeline and invite the very strike the regime cannot absorb. The IRGC gets the sea, the clerics get the nuclear file, and the Islamic Republic survives without firing the last bullet.
decision.researchNote: Two-level games best explains this: with sanctionsReliefPending false and hardlinerPressure at 81, the domestic ratification set has collapsed to zero, so Iran freezes rather than exits — preserving international optionality while paying the coalition in visible defiance.

Signing normalization now, before Netanyahu's election and with no Palestinian deliverable, would hand the religious establishment a legitimacy grievance in exchange for a deal that may not survive the Israeli political cycle — so we pause, not refuse, and keep the American nuclear file alive. Holding production stable protects both price and our OPEC+ standing; flooding the market to punish anyone would be a wager Vision 2030 cannot afford.
decision.researchNote: Prospect theory dominates: operating in a loss frame (collapsing deal, threatened Hormuz, exposed oil infrastructure), Riyadh takes the certain moderate hedge — back-channel containment plus defensive hardening — rather than the high-variance gambles of normalization now or an oil-market intervention.

decision.reasoning: I brokered this publicly, so its collapse is a loss against a claimed gain — the prospect frame makes it rational for me to spend real capital on a risky rescue rather than bank a graceful exit, and audience costs mean visible disengagement would be read across the region as abandonment even though deal integrity is technically low enough to justify it. The escort-only carrier posture answers both horns of the alliance dilemma at once: it reassures Israel enough to blunt abandonment fears and unilateral action (entrapment), while framing the force as Hormuz-protection serves my own hegemonic interest in open oil markets regardless of what the two parties do. I cannot deliver sanctions relief with Congress unratified, so I substitute the levers I actually own — non-attack assurances, humanitarian channels, verification architecture, and Hill management — and spend diplomatic capital rather than domestic capital, since public sentiment at 45 will not sustain a bigger visible commitment.
decision.researchNote: Prospect theory dominates: operating in a loss frame relative to the publicly claimed brokering success, the US accepts a low-probability rescue bid over a certain reputational write-off, with Putnam's two-level constraint dictating that the rescue be built from executive-only instruments.
